summary: Sudden P50/P95 5xx wave from edge request-hogging causing runtime worker evictions
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:40 UTC BrightPages saw a rapid increase in 5xx responses from our hosted API. The spike correlated with sustained high connection counts from a small set of client IPs and coincided with multiple runtime worker evictions on the dedicated pool serving the customer's tenant. Impact: BrightPages reported ~35% of requests returning 502/503 over a 22-minute window; end-user experiences include failed chat completions and streaming disconnects. This is customer-impacting (dedicated tenant) and appears to be caused by request patterns that exhaust runtime worker capacity and trigger eviction/backpressure that amplifies upstream 5xx. Expected: Stable P50/P95 latency and <0.1% 5xx for steady-state traffic. Observed: P50 increased from 120ms to 2.1s, P95 from 420ms to 6.8s, and 5xx rate peaked at 34.7%.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Synthetic reproduction attempt: issue reproduced by issuing ~350 simultaneous short streaming sessions from 6 client IPs with frequent connect/disconnect (1-3s lifetimes)
2) Observe runtime pool heatmap for tenant (dedicated pool) and note worker churn/evictions around the same timestamp
3) Re-run with connection pacing (limit to 40 concurrent sessions) and observe no 5xx
4) Observe API gateway upstream health checks and connection queue lengths during reproduction
logs: api-gateway logs (2026-03-12T09:40:12Z): upstream=serving-runtime-3 status=502 reason=upstream-unavailable upstream_id=rt-3 conn_count=362
serving-runtime (rt-3) stderr (2026-03-12T09:41:05Z): eviction: worker-id=7 reason=oom-or-thrashing resident_set=2463MB kvcache_misses_high=true
k8s events: Pod rt-3 terminated (OOMKilled) 2026-03-12T09:41:10Z; Pod restart took 18s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: client-side hammering (rapid short-lived streaming sessions) exhausted runtime connection/worker bookkeeping leading to thrashing and OOMs
Correlated metrics: KV cache miss rate for tenant increased 8x during spike; worker memory footprint jittered and GC frequency increased
API gateway connection queue snapshots show backlog growth from 20->420 within 90 seconds for routes serving BrightPages
Autoscaler timing: scale-up was not triggered because policy evaluates average CPU over 60s; short spikes were not captured, leaving insufficient headroom
Found a small set of client IPs responsible for ~78% of concurrent connections (probable load-testing or misconfigured customer client), contacted customer success for traffic origin verification
Temporary mitigation: increased worker reserve via manual scaling of the dedicated pool (added +4 workers) and bumped gateway upstream timeout to reduce immediate 502s
Observed partial recovery after manual scale and rate shaping at the edge; 5xx dropped to ~3% within 12 minutes

resolution: Mitigation applied: manual scaling of dedicated runtime pool (+4 workers) and temporary edge rate-shaping for BrightPages; coordinated with customer to stop accidental stress test. Root cause: unthrottled short-lived connection spike coupled with autoscaler policy not responsive to sub-60s correlation spikes and KV cache thrashing leading to worker OOMs. Permanent fixes planned: 1) autoscaler policy change to consider high short-term connection rates (burst-aware rules), 2) introduce connection-rate guardrail per-tenant at the gateway, 3) runtime memory fragmentation investigation and host-level remediation (INT-211900), 4) update BrightPages onboarding docs to include recommended client connection patterns. Customer compensated with proactive support credit. Incident closed after verification on 2026-03-14.
